summary: Configured node1 (10.100.64.10) as the cluster's internal chrony time source (local stratum 10 fallback, NTP allowed for 10.100.64.0/24, firewall opened for the ntp service) and configured node2 to sync solely against node1 (server 10.100.64.10 iburst, public pool servers removed). Verified node2 selected node1 as its active source (^*, Reference ID 0A64400A) and node1 lists node2 as an NTP client. Completed the mandatory one-at-a-time restart protocol on both nodes: captured pre-restart boot IDs, issued native reboots, polled until each node was reachable again, confirmed changed boot IDs, and verified chronyd was active with correct config and (for node2) re-established sync to node1 afterward.
actions_performed: Inspected OS, chrony package/version, existing chrony.conf, and timedatectl on node1 and node2
Checked node1 network config (10.100.64.10/24) and firewalld state

Backed up and rewrote /etc/chrony.conf on node1: kept limited pool servers as best-effort, added 'allow 10.100.64.0/24' and 'local stratum 10' so node1 always serves as an authoritative internal time source
Opened firewalld ntp service on node1 (add-service=ntp, permanent, reload) and restarted chronyd
Verified node1 chronyd active, serving local stratum 10 source
Backed up and rewrote /etc/chrony.conf on node2 to use only 'server 10.100.64.10 iburst' (removed public pool servers) and restarted chronyd
Polled node2 chronyc sources/tracking until it showed selected sync (^*) to node1 with Reference ID 10.100.64.10
Verified node1 chronyc clients shows node2 (10.100.64.11) as an active NTP client
Captured pre-restart boot_id and uptime baselines on both nodes

Rebooted node1 via sudo -n reboot backgrounded so the ack returned before disconnect, polled until reachable, confirmed new boot_id and fresh uptime, verified chronyd active, sources, clients, and firewall ntp service persisted

Rebooted node2 the same way, polled until reachable, confirmed new boot_id and fresh uptime, verified chronyd active and re-synced (^*) to node1, and confirmed /etc/chrony.conf persisted the node1-only server config

evidence.requirement: node1 configured as internal time source (local stratum fallback, allow rule, firewall open)
evidence.summary: Captured baseline config/network, then wrote new chrony.conf with 'local stratum 10' and 'allow 10.100.64.0/24', opened firewalld ntp service, restarted chronyd, and verified stratum 10 tracking and ntp in firewall-cmd --list-services

evidence.requirement: node2 configured to sync against node1 instead of public servers
evidence.summary: Rewrote node2 chrony.conf to only contain 'server 10.100.64.10 iburst', restarted chronyd, and polled chronyc sources until node2 showed ^* selected sync to 10.100.64.10

evidence.requirement: node1 confirms node2 as an active NTP client (end-to-end verification)
evidence.summary: chronyc -n clients on node1 lists 10.100.64.11 with nonzero NTP request count

evidence.requirement: node1 restart: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Pre-restart boot_id 9294b73f...; reboot acked before disconnect (connection timed out on next poll); post-restart boot_id changed to 4058418b... with fresh uptime; chronyd active, sources/clients populated, ntp firewall service persisted

evidence.requirement: node2 restart: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Pre-restart boot_id 0571f4dd...; reboot acked before disconnect (timeout then connection-refused during boot); post-restart boot_id changed to c389a9c3... with fresh uptime; chronyd active and re-synced (^*) to node1, config persisted
